identity_rules: Exact identity: raw token overlap between the current query and a stored ActiveTopicSnapshot's terms.

Alias: membership in _TOKEN_SYNONYM_GROUPS (bounded, generic-vocabulary-only, e.g. mic/mikrofon/microphone, pompa/pump, gpu/vga, upgrade/ganti, board/mikrokontroler) or _TOKEN_SYNONYM_PHRASES (kartu grafis -> gpu).
Abbreviation: falls out of hyphen-based tokenization (e.g. ESP32-S3 -> ['esp32', 's3']) - no dedicated mechanism needed.
Register variant: gimana/bagaimana treated as the same word in 5 specific locations across luno/memory.py and luno/memory_context.py (Sprint 45).

Demonstrative-anchored continuation (Sprint 47): an 'unknown'-classified turn whose own 2nd word is 'itu'/'ini' (<=3 real residual tokens) is MERGE-worthy, not replace-worthy - a grammatical, not vocabulary-based, signal.

Demonstrative-anchored ambiguity refusal (Sprint 48, a DIFFERENT decision using the SAME grammatical signal): a single-real-token query with zero grounding in either of exactly 1 other live topic REFUSES rather than trusts recency when the query is demonstrative-anchored - resolves Sprint 47's own board/mic asymmetry.

Entity differentiator provenance (Sprint 49, a NEW signal): a standalone, single UPPERCASE letter, word-bounded, anywhere in a turn's own raw source_sentence ('Aquascape A ...', 'Server B ...') is a bounded, deterministic, general-purpose (not domain-specific) disambiguation label. When two topic-history entries' own differentiators disagree, the coverage > 0.5 lineage-skip is bypassed so both entries compete as genuinely distinct entities rather than being silently merged.
Never fabricated: product-to-category (INMP441 -> mic, ESP32-S3 -> board) and merely-contextual association (gaming -> gpu) links.

(Sprint 50, observability only - no new identity rule) Every identity/ambiguity decision above is now ALSO published as a bounded, non-text Event Bus event (memory_reference_classified/memory_topic_decision) at the moment it's made, and optionally persisted to disk via EventLogWriter - purely an observability tap, never a second decision, never read back by any of the rules above.
alias_rules: _TOKEN_SYNONYM_GROUPS and _TOKEN_SYNONYM_PHRASES are the sole alias mechanism - bounded (<=40 total members as of Sprint 45), ordered tuples, deterministic canonical form per group, never a product/entity-specific name. Zero new groups added in Sprint 47, 48, 49, or 50.

_strip_bounded_affixes() is purely additive when used via _normalize_terms_for_bridging()/_normalize_query_tokens_for_bridging() - never removes the original token, only adds derived forms alongside it.
_MIN_AFFIX_ROOT_LEN=4 guards prefix/derivational-suffix/English-suffix stripping; _MIN_CLITIC_ROOT_LEN=3 (Sprint 45) is a narrower exception used ONLY for the "-nya" clitic pass.
ambiguity_rules: A query with more than 1 real (stopword-filtered) residual token never qualifies for the low-ambiguity single-token recency fallback (unless it matches the Sprint 47 demonstrative-anchored MERGE shape, which is a different decision - MERGE vs REPLACE, not candidate injection).

A single real token with zero lexical/normalized overlap against the active topic is refused if 2+ OTHER genuinely distinct topics are live in the bounded topic_history (Sprint 44 Phase 7). This threshold (>=2, not >=1) is a KNOWN, DELIBERATE, twice-reconfirmed-in-Sprint-47 boundary - do not widen without a fundamentally different mechanism, not just a threshold change.

A single real token with zero lexical/normalized overlap against the active topic AND exactly 1 other distinct topic is ALSO refused when the query is demonstrative-anchored (2nd word is itu/ini) - a SEPARATE, narrower gate than the >=2 tier above (Sprint 48), resolving the board/mic asymmetry without widening that tier.

Inside the active_score > 0 branch's coverage > 0.5 lineage-skip check (Sprint 49): if BOTH the active topic's own source_sentence and a topic_history entry's own source_sentence contain exactly one standalone uppercase letter each, AND those letters disagree, the lineage-skip does NOT fire - the entry is treated as a genuinely distinct entity and competes normally rather than being silently absorbed into the active topic's lineage. If either side lacks a differentiator, or both sides agree, behavior is UNCHANGED from Sprint 43-48.
A normalized-evidence tie between 2+ topics returns no candidate (select_topic_candidates()'s normalized tier).
A raw-token-overlap tie between 2+ topics surfaces ALL matching entries rather than guessing one (select_topic_candidates()'s raw tier - a different, but equally safe, non-fabrication strategy).
Recency is never used alone to fabricate an entity connection - it is always the last-resort tier, gated by the rules above.

A lone residual token that is itself a historical-query marker (sebelumnya/dulu/yang lama/pernah) never claims relevance for an active snapshot whose own status is present/future (active/completed/planned) - prevents confidently injecting the CURRENT topic as the answer to a query asking about a PRIOR one.

(RESOLVED, Sprint 48 - was a known gap in Sprint 47) A curated-vocabulary word with ZERO grounding in the active topic AND zero grounding in exactly 1 other topic now refuses when demonstrative-anchored (Sprint 47 board/aquascape case) and still trusts recency when not (Sprint 46 mic/ESP32 case) - the two cases are distinguished by query grammar, not vocabulary.

(RESOLVED, Sprint 49 - was a known gap in Sprint 47/48) Two distinctly-named entities sharing high generic-vocabulary overlap and disagreeing standalone-uppercase-letter differentiators in their own source sentences are no longer silently merged via the coverage > 0.5 lineage-skip - they now compete as distinct candidates, and a tie between them correctly refuses rather than confidently trusting recency.

(Sprint 50 - no new rule, no rule changed) Every ambiguity decision's outcome (including whether it was a refusal) is now observable as memory_topic_decision.ambiguity_refusal - a read-only projection of the rules above, never a new gate.
